To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a scanning strategy is proposed for selective laser melting of the Ti-6Al4V alloy which provides a uniform microstructure of α + β lamellae along the building direction and that a 3D network of β is generated in regions highly exposed to an intensified intrinsic heat-treatment.
an intensified intrinsic heat-treatment is applied during selective-laser-melting of Ti-64V, resulting in a uniform, fine α + β micro-structure.
a selective laser melting-manufacturer can be designed to simultaneously produce and heat treat a titanium alloy part.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new processing route to obtain stable α + β microstructures in Ti-6Al4V components produced by selective laser melting.
the development of an intensified intrinsic heat-treatment strategy during selective laser melting that allows manufacturing of components with a stable microstructure in a single-step process.
a new approach to the manufacturing of Ti-6A-4V parts using selective laser melting that combines porosity optimization with an intensified intrinsic heat-treatment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

a combination of porosity-optimized scanning and a very tight hatch spacing is a viable strategy to induce stable α + β microstructures with a high degree of stabilization in selective laser melting of the Ti-6Al–4V alloy.
the intensified intrinsic heat treatments applied in this work provide a viable solution for the fabrication of high-strength Ti-6Al-V parts using selective laser melting.
the application of the intensified intrinsic heat treatments during selective laser melting processing of Ti-6-Al-4V powder results in a stable α + β microstructural state.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the intensified intrinsic heat treatments can be used for the selective laser melting of titanium alloys to induce microstructures with a high degree of stabilization, and that this can be used to improve the mechanical properties of manufactured parts.
the selective laser melting-manufacturer is also a heat treater.
the intensified intrinsic heat treatments can be used as a tool to tailor the microstructure of Ti-6AL-4V during selective laser melting.
The main takeaway from our work is that
selective laser melting-manu-facturing and heat treatment can be combined to produce parts with stable microstructures, thus avoiding post-manufacturing heat treatment.

the intensified intrinsic heat treatments can be applied during selective laser melt manufacturing in order to obtain a uniform, stable microstructure in the final component, which is a key requirement for structural applications.
a combination of porosity-optimized selective laser melting processing and an intensified intrinsic heat-treatment can be applied for manufacturing Ti-6Al4V parts with stable α + β microstructures.
